chunks: And with this chain of narration, from Ja'far, from his father, upon them be peace, who said:

The first to fight was Ibrahim (peace be upon him), when the Romans captured Lut (peace be upon him), so Ibrahim (peace be upon him) set out until he rescued him from their hands. And the first to throw an arrow in the cause of Allah was Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, may Allah curse him. And the first to tether a horse in the cause of Allah was Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad, may Allah have mercy on him. And the first martyr in Islam was Mihsa. And the first to spur the horse in the cause of Allah was Ja'far ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon him), the Two-Winged One, who spurred his horse. And the first to adopt the banner 'La ilaha illa Allah' was Ibrahim (peace be upon him).
ai.seo_question: Who was the first martyr in Islam and who was the first to fight among the prophets?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahid al-Ahkam* establishes a hierarchy of martial precedence in Islamic tradition, attributing the first instance of fighting to Prophet Ibrahim and the first martyr to Mihsa. It specifically highlights Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas as the first archer, a distinction often linked to the Battle of Badr, while identifying Ja'far ibn Abi Talib as the first to spur his horse, emphasizing his role as 'Dhul-Janaḥayn' in early cavalry engagements.
